name: Oriented Diameter
definition: The **oriented diameter** $\mathrm{D}^+(\mathcal{H})$ of a family $\mathcal{H}$ is defined as $$ \mathrm{D}^+(\mathcal{H}):= \max\{|S\|: \{\emptyset, S\}\subset \mathcal{H}\_{|S}} $$
graph_summary: The largest set supporting both the all-zero and all-one traces.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: Every oriented-diameter witness in a subfamily is also a witness in the containing class.

p_monotonic.proof: Projecting an oriented-diameter witness only deletes coordinates, so it cannot increase its length.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Counterexample to strict c-monotonicity: for $\mathcal H=\{0010,0100,0111,1001\}$, conditioning the second coordinate gives two fibres of oriented diameter 2, while $\mathrm D^+(\mathcal H)=2$. Thus the full value does not strictly exceed the smaller fibre value.
